WinGet CLI

Please add the following maintenance commands to WinGet:

1. winget autoremove : Remove unused dependencies.
2. winget clean: Clean temporary files and old installer data.
3. winget cache: Show cache size and location.
4. winget cache list: List cached installers.
5. winget cache remove: Remove cache for a specific package.
6. winget cache purge: Remove all cached installers.

- Saves disk space.
- Simplifies package maintenance.
- Better for power users and developers.

- Support --whatif for previewing changes.

winget autoremove --whatif winget clean --whatif winget cache purge --whatif

Add:

winget doctor

Checks:

- Corrupted cache
- Broken package registrations
- Source issues
- Installation problems

items.title: [Bug] uninstall_xfce.sh purges openssl and takes ca-certificates, python3-pip and ruby with it (42 packages removed)
items.body:
### Summary

`uninstall_xfce.sh` passes `openssl` to `apt-get purge`. On a Debian chroot that is not a leaf package, so removing it cascades into `ca-certificates`, `python3-pip`, `python3-requests`, `ruby`, `bundler` and `snapd`. The follow-up `apt-get autoremove -y` then takes the rest. What the user expects to be "remove the VNC server" ends up removing **42 packages** and leaves the chroot without working TLS — `pip`, `gem` and anything else that validates certificates stop working, and that failure shows up much later, with no obvious connection to the VNC uninstall.

### Environment

- Stryker 6.5.1 (versionCode 651), root mode
- LineageOS 23.2 / Android 16, arm64, Redmi Note 10 Pro (sweet)
- Debian chroot at `/data/local/stryker/release`
- `uninstall_xfce.sh` as shipped in `app/src/main/assets/` on `main` (verified byte-identical to the copy extracted on device)

### Reproduction

Settings → VNC server → Uninstall, or directly:

```bash
apt-get purge -y openssl xvfb x11vnc xfce4 xfce4-session xfce4-panel xfdesktop4 \
    xfwm4 xfconf xfce4-terminal elementary-xfce-icon-theme dbus-x11
apt-get autoremove -y
```

### Evidence

`apt-get purge -s` with the exact package list from the script:

```
The following packages will be REMOVED:
  bundler* ca-certificates* dbus-x11* elementary-xfce-icon-theme* exo-utils*
  libgarcon-gtk3-1-0* libruby* libruby3.3* libthunarx-3-0*
  libxfce4panel-2.0-4* libxfce4ui-2-0* libxfce4ui-utils* libxfconf-0-3* novnc*
  openssl* python3-certifi* python3-pip* python3-requests* python3-websockify*
  rake* ruby* ruby-bundler* ruby-dev* ruby-rubygems* ruby3.3* ruby3.3-dev*
  rubygems-integration* snapd* thunar* websockify* x11vnc* xfce4*
  xfce4-appfinder* xfce4-panel* xfce4-pulseaudio-plugin* xfce4-session*
  xfce4-settings* xfce4-terminal* xfconf* xfdesktop4* xfwm4* xvfb*
0 upgraded, 0 newly installed, 42 to remove and 38 not upgraded.
```

Note that `novnc`, `websockify` and `python3-websockify` are in there too, so the browser-based access that `install_xfce.sh` sets up is collateral damage as well.

### Suggested fix

1. Drop `openssl` from the purge list. `install_xfce.sh` installs `ca-certificates curl openssl` as prerequisites for `apt`, not as part of the desktop — they should survive an uninstall of the desktop.
2. Use `--no-autoremove`, or replace the blanket `apt-get autoremove -y` with an explicit list, so the dependency solver cannot reach outside the XFCE set.
3. Optionally run `apt-get purge -s` first and show the resulting list to the user before committing, since the chroot is shared with everything else the user has installed.

A minimal change that fixes the cascade:

```diff
-apt-get purge -y openssl xvfb x11vnc xfce4 xfce4-session xfce4-panel xfdesktop4 \
+apt-get purge -y --no-autoremove xvfb x11vnc xfce4 xfce4-session xfce4-panel xfdesktop4 \
     xfwm4 xfconf xfce4-terminal elementary-xfce-icon-theme dbus-x11 || deleting_packages_error
-apt-get autoremove -y || deleting_packages_error
```

### Secondary, smaller point

The final `rm -rf` line removes `/root/.cache`, `/root/.config` and `/root/.local` wholesale. Those directories are shared with every other tool in the chroot, not just XFCE, so an uninstall of the VNC server also discards unrelated configuration. Narrowing it to the XFCE-specific subdirectories (`/root/.config/xfce4`, `/root/.config/Thunar`, `/root/.local/share/xfce4`, `/root/.vnc`) would be safer.

### Not a bug, for the record

The current `install_xfce.sh` on `main` is in good shape on this device — `-noshm` for `x11vnc`, the explicit `WxHxD` resolution and the `libgl1-mesa-dri` / `procps` additions all do the right thing inside the chroot. The uninstall path is the one that did not get the same attention.

items.title: Decide what happens to old kernel packages across a version bump, and test the upgrade path

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: question
labels.description: Further information is requested

items.body:
`qcom-next` has just moved from 7.2 to 7.3 (the `qcom-next-7.3-*` Release ref bumps, most recently 4d67aec), and `qcom-7.2` is still shipped as a separate variant. We have no written policy for the packages a bump leaves behind, and no test that a device on the old packages actually upgrades to the new ones.

## How it works today

Each build produces versioned packages, `linux-image-<KVER>`, `linux-headers-<KVER>` and `linux-image-<KVER>-dbg`. It also produces the metapackages `linux-image-<variant>` and `linux-headers-<variant>`, which depend on exactly that KVER. The variant name is part of KVER, so every snapshot is a new package that installs alongside the earlier ones rather than replacing them (see `docs/version.md`).

That gives two different cases:

1. **Within a variant** (e.g. `qcom-next` 7.2 → 7.3). The metapackage keeps its name and its version goes up. `apt upgrade` should pull in the 7.3 image and leave the 7.2 one for autoremove.
2. **Across variants** (e.g. `qcom-7.2` → a future `qcom-7.3`, or `qcom-7.2` → `qcom-next`). `linux-image-qcom-7.2` is a different package from anything that replaces it. A device that has it installed will never move off 7.2 unless the user changes packages by hand.

## Questions

- **Archive retention.** How long do old `linux-image-<KVER>` builds stay in the `qli` workspace (and staging)? Keep all of them, keep the last N per variant, or drop a series once it has been replaced?
- **Retiring a variant.** When `qcom-7.2` (and `qcom-7.2-debug`) is retired, what happens to its metapackages?
  - Keep publishing the final build forever, unchanged.
  - Ship a last transitional `linux-image-qcom-7.2` that depends on its successor, so `apt upgrade` moves devices over.
  - Something else, e.g. stop at the last build and document the manual switch.
- **Which successor.** If there is a transition, does a fixed series move to the next fixed series (`qcom-7.3`), or to `qcom-next`?
- **DKMS/modules packages.** Do they follow the image across the transition (`<name>-modules-<KVER>` and their metapackage; see `debian/README.md`)?
- **On the device.** Does autoremove behave for these packages, i.e. the running kernel and the newest one are kept and older ones are removable?

## Make sure there is an upgrade path

Whatever we decide, CI should prove it rather than rely on version ordering on paper. For example, an install test per suite that:

1. installs the previous Release metapackages (and DKMS modules) for a variant,
2. adds the new build and runs `apt full-upgrade`,
3. checks that the new kernel is installed and is the boot default, that the modules for it are present, and that the old kernel is offered for autoremove.

The same test can cover a variant transition once we have one (`qcom-7.2` → its successor), and the 7.2 → 7.3 move inside `qcom-next` is a good first case to check by hand now.

items.title: [packaging] documentdb-setup, reset and package removal report success that isn't true

labels.name: documentdb-1.0
labels.description: Stable release

labels.name: 1.0-blocker
labels.description: Must be fixed before the 1.0 release

items.body:
Several day-2 paths in the native install exit 0 while the system is not in the state they report. Mostly non-systemd hosts. Related: #727, #732.

**Items**
- [ ] documentdb-setup: pg_ctl restart path omits -l, so the new postmaster keeps setup's stdout and hangs piped callers
- [ ] documentdb-setup (non-systemd): scoped --restore and --status ignore the recorded gateway PID, so success/health can be false
- [ ] Reset and package removal report success while PostgreSQL or the gateway is still running (non-systemd)
- [ ] documentdb-setup re-run resets DOCUMENTDB_LISTEN_ADDR to a wildcard bind and never updates documentdb_core
- [ ] documentdb-setup configures a major with no documentdb-N package; apt autoremove can then remove a running install
- [ ] documentdb-gateway --check reports OK when pg_hba/pg_ident changes haven't been reloaded

### 1. documentdb-setup: pg_ctl restart path omits -l, so the new postmaster keeps setup's stdout and hangs piped callers

On non-systemd hosts, when PostgreSQL is already running and the config changed (e.g. re-running with `--restore`, or `DOCUMENTDB_TOAST_COMPRESSION` changed), `documentdb-setup` restarts it with:

```
documentdb-local/scripts/documentdb-setup.sh:3078
run_as_user documentdb-local "${PG_CTL}" -D "${DATA_DIR}" -w restart      # no -l
```

while the start path at :3084 passes `-l "${DATA_DIR}/pglog.log"`. Without `-l` the new postmaster inherits setup's stdout/stderr. Setup prints `SUCCESS: DocumentDB is ready` and exits, but the pipe stays open, so any caller reading it (`| tee`, `| cat`, `$(...)`, CI log capture) blocks until timeout. A minimal `pg_ctl restart | cat` without `-l` times out; with `-l` it returns.

Side effects: PG log lines leak into the caller's stdout/file instead of `pglog.log`, which the setup hint at :3804 points users to.

Related: the gateway fallback launch (:3602) uses `nohup ... &` without `setsid`, so it stays in the caller's process group. When the hung caller is Ctrl-C'd or hit by a CI timeout SIGTERM, the gateway gets the signal too and the service ends up down after a success message.

Fix: add `-l "${DATA_DIR}/pglog.log"` to the restart at :3078, and consider `setsid` for the gateway launch (check the pidfile/exe-match logic still holds). A regression test could run the restart path with stdout piped to `cat` under a timeout.

### 2. documentdb-setup (non-systemd): scoped --restore and --status ignore the recorded gateway PID, so success/health can be false

Without systemd, `documentdb-setup` writes a per-port record at gateway launch (`nohup_gateway_pid_for_port`) but several paths ignore it. Static read of `documentdb-local/scripts/documentdb-setup.sh` on main:

1. **Scoped `--restore --pg-version N`** (:4852) skips the nohup sweep, deletes `setup.conf`, then prints "Restore complete" and exits 0 (:4884). The gateway keeps serving and can no longer be located via state. The recorded port isn't read first.
2. **`--status`** (:4240) reports `active (nohup; no systemd)` whenever anything listens on the port, with no PID/exe check, and exits 0 if mode is configured. A foreign listener reads as healthy.
3. **`--listen-port` change** (`start_gateway`, :3433 onward) only inspects the new port; the previously persisted port's gateway keeps running. The restore comment at :4796 describes this exact two-gateway outcome.
4. When `find_listener_pid` returns the "1" placeholder (:543-585) and no record exists, setup dies with `die_unknown_listener_owner` even with lsof/ss installed; there's no cmdline fallback.

Fix sketch: in scoped restore, read the major's `GATEWAY_PORT`, stop the recorded PID, and `die` non-zero if it can't be stopped. In `--status`, require a live recorded PID with a matching exe. In `start_gateway`, stop the old persisted port's recorded gateway on change.

Scope decisions:
- Sub-item 3 under `--no-enable`: setup leaves the old port's gateway running and warns with the port. `--no-enable` means "don't change the gateway's running state"; stopping it would leave nothing listening on either port.
- Sub-item 4 is deferred to its own change. A cmdline fallback can't tell which major owns the port on a multi-major host (every gateway has the same command line except its config path), so it risks stopping another major's gateway. A correct fix needs config-path matching. Until then setup keeps failing with a clear error rather than guessing.

Related: #727.

### 3. Reset and package removal report success while PostgreSQL or the gateway is still running (non-systemd)

On a host without systemd, three teardown paths exit 0 while a postmaster or gateway keeps running. Related to #727, which covers only `documentdb-setup --restore`.

1. `documentdb-local-reset --confirm-destroy`: `documentdb-local/scripts/documentdb-local-reset.sh:232-250` only runs `pg_ctl stop` and the live-postmaster check when `${data_dir}/postmaster.pid` exists. If the data dir is already gone, or the major was never installed, both are skipped. The `[[ -d ]]`-guarded removals (253-285) become no-ops and line 294 prints "completely reset" regardless. Repro: `documentdb-setup`, `rm -rf /var/lib/documentdb-local/18/data`, then reset prints success and exits 0 while the postgres process and port 9718 are still up. A never-installed major also reports success.

2. DEB `prerm` for `documentdb-N` (`packaging/standalone/build-standalone-deb.sh:236-250`) and the gateway `prerm` (`documentdb-local/maintainer-scripts/gateway/prerm:24-33`) only stop things when systemd is present. The RPM `%preun` in `packaging/rpm/spec/documentdb-gateway.spec:146-162` has the same gate. `apt purge` therefore leaves the nohup gateway and postgres serving from deleted binaries and config.

3. `autoremove` can drop `documentdb-gateway` while it keeps serving, same cause.

Suggested fix: reset locates the postmaster without relying on `PGDATA` (the pid file, then pgrep/port), stops it, verifies nothing is left, and prints a distinct message when there is nothing to reset. On non-systemd hosts, `prerm` stops the processes it started (fast, then immediate shutdown) and warns if one survives.

Scope decision: removal never refuses. That matches the systemd branch of the same scripts (`systemctl stop ... || true`) and Debian's postgresql packages. A process that survives an immediate shutdown is usually mid-checkpoint, where blocking `apt`/`dnf` and telling the operator to kill it is worse than a warning.

### 4. documentdb-setup re-run resets DOCUMENTDB_LISTEN_ADDR to a wildcard bind and never updates documentdb_core

Two silent day-2 problems in `documentdb-setup` re-runs.

**1. Re-run overwrites a restricted bind address.** `default_gateway_settings_from_persisted_state` (`documentdb-local/scripts/documentdb-setup.sh:2243`) restores only the port and TLS keys. Then `documentdb-setup.sh:2364` always passes `--listen-addr ":${GATEWAY_PORT}"`, and `write_gateway_env_fragment` (`documentdb-register-gateway.sh:1230-1244`) rewrites the managed block via `rewrite_with_managed_block` (`documentdb-tools-lib.sh:371`), which appends the new block last. So `DOCUMENTDB_LISTEN_ADDR=127.0.0.1:10260` becomes `:10260` (all interfaces), exit 0, no warning. `--status` (`documentdb-setup.sh:4252-4266`) prints only the port, so the change is invisible.

**2. `documentdb_core` is never updated.** The wizard runs `ALTER EXTENSION documentdb UPDATE` (`:3235`) and `ALTER EXTENSION documentdb_extended_rum UPDATE` (`:3242`), but not `documentdb_core`. After a package upgrade plus re-run, `documentdb` moves to the new version while `documentdb_core` stays on the old catalog version. `--status` shows no extension versions either.

**Suggested fix**
- Restore the persisted `DOCUMENTDB_LISTEN_ADDR` host the same way the port/TLS are restored, with a "Keeping gateway bind address ..." log line.
- Run `ALTER EXTENSION documentdb_core UPDATE` before `documentdb` (same transaction).
- Print the bind address and installed `documentdb_core`/`documentdb`/`documentdb_extended_rum` versions in `--status`.
- Add tests for both in `documentdb_local_tests/test_documentdb_setup.py`.

Related: #732 (installer day-2 diagnostics).

### 5. documentdb-setup configures a major with no documentdb-N package; apt autoremove can then remove a running install

`documentdb-setup --pg-version N` only checks that PG binaries and `documentdb.control` exist (`documentdb-local/scripts/documentdb-setup.sh:1532`, `:2036`); the only major gate is `>= 16` (`:2591`). It never checks that `documentdb-N` is installed. Since `documentdb-common` is held only by `documentdb-N`'s Depends (`packaging/standalone/build-standalone-deb.sh`), it stays auto-installed for another major only.

Repro (Debian/Ubuntu):
```
apt-get install postgresql-17-documentdb documentdb-18
documentdb-setup ... --pg-version 17      # succeeds, gateway on 10260
apt-get purge --autoremove documentdb-18 postgresql-18-documentdb
```
`documentdb-common`, gateway and tools get autoremoved. The PG17 gateway keeps running from a deleted binary, and `documentdb-setup` / `documentdb-local-reset` are gone.

Also: `build-common-deb.sh:159` has an unversioned `Replaces: documentdb-16, documentdb-17, documentdb-18` with no `Breaks`, so apt offers `documentdb-common` as a substitute for a missing `documentdb-N`. The comment above it says the pre-split package never shipped.

Suggested fix:
- In setup, require `documentdb-<major>` (dpkg-query / rpm -q) when `documentdb-common` is package-managed; die or warn.
- Drop that `Replaces`, or pair it with a `Breaks`.
- Optionally `apt-mark manual documentdb-common` at setup.

### 6. documentdb-gateway --check reports OK when pg_hba/pg_ident changes haven't been reloaded

`documentdb-gateway --check` can print `check OK` and exit 0 while every client request would fail peer authentication.

**Why:** `run_check` (`pg_documentdb_gw/documentdb_gateway/src/check.rs:27-62`) calls `create_connection_pool_manager`, whose `validate_startup_pools` (`pool_manager.rs:387-396`) only touches the SystemRequests and PreAuthRequests pools. Those connect as `postgres_system_user` (`pool_manager.rs:332-345`), i.e. the URL-file role, which works with plain same-name peer auth before any reload. `check.rs` then queries `pg_extension` on that same system pool.

Client requests use a different path: `allocate_data_pool` (`auth.rs:576`, `auth.rs:770`, `context/connection.rs:245-254`) connects as the authenticated user, relying on the managed `peer map=documentdb-gateway-map` rule written by `documentdb-local/scripts/documentdb-register-gateway.sh:420`. That rule is only active after a PostgreSQL reload, which the script just prints as a remaining step (`:695`, `:742`). `--check` never exercises it.

**Repro:** run `documentdb-register-gateway`, skip the reload, run `documentdb-gateway --check` (OK), then connect with a client (peer auth failure).

`packaging/gateway/packaging-design.md:166` claims a green `--check` "strongly implies a successful service start"; not true here. `test-gateway-install-entrypoint.sh` only checks the happy path after reload.

**Fix idea:** after the system-pool query, open a throwaway data-pool connection as a role covered by the managed hba/ident entries (e.g. a member of `documentdb_admin_role`) and run `SELECT 1`. On failure, print the role and hint at `systemctl reload postgresql@<N>-<cluster>`. Add a negative test: register, no reload, `--check` must fail; reload, must pass.

items.title: The ice-all metapackages break the 3.7 to 3.8 Linux package upgrade
items.body:
Upgrading a 3.7 host to 3.8 works when the packages were installed by name: swap the repo configuration, run the upgrade command, restart the registry. It breaks when the host was installed through `ice-all-runtime` or `ice-all-devel`, which is what our install docs tell people to use. The metapackages pull in `icepatch2` and `ice-compilers`, which nothing in 3.8 obsoletes, and their 3.8 transitional replacements depend on nothing, so dnf and apt treat every Ice package as an orphan afterwards.

These results come from scripted container runs driven by an AI assistant and have not been reproduced by hand yet. Please verify each item before acting on it.

Setup: Rocky 9 and Debian 12 (arm64), Ice 3.7.11 installed from `ice-all-runtime`, the registry enabled and running with an edited `icegridregistry.conf`, and an application deployed. Each path started from that state in a fresh container with the 3.8 repo configured.

**Metapackage installs**

- `dnf upgrade` refuses to resolve: the installed `icepatch2` 3.7 requires `ice-utils = 3.7.x` and no 3.8 package obsoletes it. `dnf upgrade --allowerasing` gets through by erasing it.
- With `ice-all-devel` installed, `ice-compilers` 3.7 pins `ice-slice` the same way and `--allowerasing` cannot resolve it. The 3.8 spec's `ice-compilers` stub has no `%package` line, so its tags land in the description of `ice-all-devel` and the package that should obsolete the 3.7 one is never built.
- After any upgrade, every Ice package is an orphan because the transitional `ice-all-runtime` depends on nothing. The next `dnf autoremove` or `apt autoremove` removes `icegrid`. Upgrading only the metapackage sets the same trap without upgrading anything else.
- `apt upgrade` replaces only the metapackage and `zeroc-ice-slice` and holds the service packages back; `apt full-upgrade` upgrades everything and leaves `zeroc-icepatch2` 3.7 installed.
- The 3.8.3 EL9 repo has no transitional packages; `ice-all-runtime` and `ice-all-devel` stop at 3.8.2 although the v3.8.3 spec defines them.

**By-name installs**

- A host with `icegrid` installed by name has no `icepatch2` and keeps `icegrid` marked as explicitly installed. `dnf upgrade` and `apt full-upgrade` complete, and autoremove only drops `libice3.7-c++` and `libicestorm3.7`. This is inferred from the run that marked `icegrid` and removed `icepatch2` and the metapackage before upgrading, which is the same state.

**All installs, after the upgrade**

- The registry is not restarted. The 3.7 RPM postun marks `icegriregistry.service`, the typo fixed by #6903 (#6904), and the DEB upgrade does not restart it either. The 3.7 process keeps running from a deleted binary until the next restart, which is when 3.7 nodes stop working.
- An unchanged 3.7 `icegridregistry.conf` is replaced by the 3.8 stock file, which drops `IceGrid.InstanceName`, so the locator becomes `IceGrid/Locator`, and opens the client and server endpoints on all interfaces. An edited config is kept; on DEB it triggers dpkg's conffile prompt, which errors out in a non-interactive run.
- A 3.7 config that sets a removed property, such as `IceGrid.Registry.SessionTimeout`, stops the 3.8 registry from starting.
- The 3.8 registry opens the 3.7 database without migration, as the upgrade guide says.

**Repo packages**

- DEB: `ice-repo-3.7` and `ice-repo-3.8` both ship `/usr/share/keyrings/zeroc-archive-keyring.gpg`, so the 3.8 package cannot be installed until the 3.7 one is removed, and the 3.8 repo is signed with a different key.
- RPM: the two repo packages install side by side, so a host that adds the 3.8 repo gets the major upgrade on its next routine `dnf upgrade`.

**To decide**

- Should a 3.8 package obsolete `icepatch2` and the 3.7 `ice-compilers`, so the plain upgrade command resolves for metapackage installs?
- Should the transitional `ice-all-runtime` and `ice-all-devel` depend on the 3.8 package set, so autoremove cannot take the registry? Or should we drop the metapackages and document by-name installs?
- Should `ice-repo-3.8` conflict with `ice-repo-3.7` on both RPM and DEB, so a host is never on both channels at once?
- Should the upgrade restart the registry, and should the docs state the registry and node upgrade order?
- Should the 3.8 stock registry config keep an instance name and the localhost-only endpoints that 3.7 shipped?
- Should the upgrade guide gain a Linux packages section covering the repo swap, `full-upgrade`, and the restart?

This morning's automatic upgrade uninstalled Proton VPN. The Proton repository had just published `python3-proton-vpn-api-core` 6.1.1, which declares

```
Breaks: proton-vpn-cli (<< 1.0.6~rc202610161029), proton-vpn-daemon (<< 0.14.0), proton-vpn-gtk-app (<< 4.18.9~rc202610161032), python3-proton-vpn-network-manager (<< 0.13.5)
```

The matching app versions only appeared in the repository 13 minutes later. The automatic run happened in between and resolved the conflict by removing the app. From `/var/log/mintupdate.log`:

```
-- Automatic Upgrade starting Mon 02 Nov 2026 09:57:30 CET:
[...]
The following packages will be REMOVED:
```

items.title: documentdb-setup configures majors with no owning package; autoremove then dismantles a running install
items.body:
## Summary

`documentdb-setup --pg-version N` builds a complete, working appliance for a major whose `documentdb-N` package is **not installed**. Nothing then owns that install, so a later `apt autoremove` deletes the shared payload — `documentdb-setup`, `documentdb-local-reset`, the gateway binary — out from under a **running, network-exposed** service.

## Reproduction

```bash
# repos configured per https://documentdb.io/docs/getting-started/packages/
apt-get install -y postgresql-17-documentdb documentdb-18
documentdb-setup --admin-user admin --admin-password-file /root/pw.txt --yes --pg-version 17
apt-get purge -y --autoremove documentdb-18 postgresql-18-documentdb   # the documented removal recipe
```

```
  documentdb-17 installed? -> not-installed
  rc=0  -> 1 success banner(s);  gateway listening on: localhost:10260
    Removing documentdb-18 / documentdb-common / documentdb-gateway
            / documentdb-postgresql-tools / postgresql-18-documentdb
===== REPRO RESULT
    /usr/bin/documentdb-gateway                          GONE
    /usr/bin/documentdb-setup                            GONE
    /usr/bin/documentdb-local-reset                      GONE
    /usr/bin/documentdb-gateway-admin                    GONE
    /etc/documentdb/gateway/SetupConfiguration.json      GONE
    PG17 gateway daemon still running: 6317
    PG17 state dir still present:      /etc/documentdb/local/17
    listener on 10260:                 2
```

The PG17 gateway keeps serving from a deleted binary, still bound to `0.0.0.0:10260` (`mongosh` returned the live document afterwards), while `documentdb-setup --status`, `--restore` and `documentdb-local-reset` are all `command not found`. **There is no shipped way to stop, manage or clean it up**, and it will not survive a reboot.

Note the operator did nothing wrong to major 17 — they removed major 18 with the documented command.

## Root cause

Ownership of `documentdb-common` is expressed **only** by `documentdb-N`. Because `documentdb-17` was never installed, nothing held the dependency, so `--autoremove` reaped the shared payload.

The enabling condition is that `documentdb-setup --pg-version 17` succeeded at all, with `documentdb-17` absent:

```
dpkg -S /etc/documentdb/local/17/setup.conf
dpkg-query: no path found matching pattern /etc/documentdb/local/17/setup.conf
```

## Same cause: PostgreSQL 16

The docs state PG 16 is extension-only — *"no gateway, no `documentdb-setup`, no systemd units"*. In fact:

```bash
documentdb-setup --admin-user admin --admin-password-file /root/pw.txt --yes --pg-version 16
RC=0
```
```
PG16 catalog:  documentdb = 0.114-0 / documentdb_core = 0.114-0 / documentdb_extended_rum = 0.114-0
Gateway:       documentdb-gateway 0.116.0
listener:      10260  (mode: greenfield, both services active)
PG16 appliance CRUD: [{"_id":"...","pg":16}]
```

A 0.116 gateway serving a 0.114 catalog on an explicitly unsupported major, with no warning.

## Related packaging defect

`documentdb-common` declares `Replaces: documentdb-16, documentdb-17, documentdb-18` with **no `Breaks:`/`Conflicts:`**, so APT actively suggests it as a substitute:

```
Package documentdb-16 is not available, but is referred to by another package.
However the following packages replace it:
  documentdb-common
E: Package 'documentdb-16' has no installation candidate
```

Following that suggestion installs `documentdb-common` + `documentdb-gateway` + `documentdb-postgresql-tools` — the wizard, the daemon and every systemd template — with no PostgreSQL and no extension.

## Suggested fix

- Have `documentdb-setup` refuse, or loudly warn, when `documentdb-<major>` is not installed for the major being configured.
- Add `Breaks:` alongside `documentdb-common`'s `Replaces:` so APT stops recommending it as a substitute.
- Consider having the per-major setup drop a marker that makes the dependency explicit, so `autoremove` cannot reap a payload still in use.

Found by adversarial multi-major testing of the published 0.116 packages.

items.title: Mark All Upgrades removes desktop and networking packages during phased systemd update
items.body:
### Environment

- Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS (resolute), amd64
- Synaptic 0.91.7build1; APT 3.2.0
- Observed on 2026-10-27 and reproduced on 2026-10-29 while systemd/udev 259.9-0ubuntu0.1 was being phased. Some components remained at 259.5-0ubuntu3.4.

### What happened

On 2026-10-27, a Synaptic upgrade transaction upgraded `libnss-systemd` to 259.9-0ubuntu0.1 and removed 55 packages, including `ubuntu-desktop`, `ubuntu-minimal`, `network-manager`, `netplan.io`, `snapd`, `firefox`, `xorg`, and `initramfs-tools`. The APT history records `Commandline: /usr/sbin/synaptic` for this transaction. A subsequent `apt autoremove` removed more packages. Network access and browsers disappeared.

After reinstalling the missing packages, Synaptic's **Mark All Upgrades** again proposed removing dozens of installed packages, including `ubuntu-desktop`, `network-manager`, `netplan.io`, `snapd`, `firefox`, and Xorg components. These were proposed dependency changes; none were manually marked for removal. The behavior continued until the systemd/udev packages were upgraded together.

### Solver comparison at the time of reproduction

- `apt-get -s -o APT::Solver=internal dist-upgrade` reproduced the large removal proposal.
- `apt-get -s dist-upgrade` with APT 3.2's default solver proposed only the unrelated removal of `lsb-invalid-mta`.
- `apt-get -s -o APT::Solver=internal -o APT::Get::Always-Include-Phased-Updates=true dist-upgrade` proposed zero removals.
- `Debug::pkgProblemResolver=yes` showed the internal solver attempting to upgrade systemd libraries while deferring `systemd-sysv` / `udev`, then choosing to remove `udev` and cascading into desktop and networking removals.

Upgrading the 13 matching systemd/udev packages from 259.5-0ubuntu3.4 to 259.9-0ubuntu0.1 resolved the issue. Afterward, the internal-solver simulation proposed zero removals, and Synaptic's Mark All Upgrades showed only expected upgrades.

### Expected behavior

When phased versions of mutually dependent systemd packages cannot be upgraded together, Mark All Upgrades should defer the conflicting upgrades or clearly block an upgrade plan that removes core desktop and networking packages.

This may be an APT internal resolver issue, but Synaptic exposes the resulting plan in its normal upgrade flow and permitted the original transaction. Related broader upgrade-solver discussions: #143 and #165.

items.title: Failure to parse apt output if < 10000 bytes
items.body:
BleachBit's regex fails in the less common scenario of output smaller than 10,000 bytes. Example outputs from apt: `Del foo 1.0-1 [1234 B]` or `After this operation, 1234 B disk space will be freed.`

Notes

- This issue is a follow up to 0c9d1b7e41fb7fe2487700724bb46b589c18880d regarding parsing output of `apt`.
- apt's logic is in function `SizeToStr`in `strutl.cc`
- apt uses base 10 (not base 2)
- apt suffixes are 'k' (lowercase) and then 'M' through 'Y' (uppercase)
- We do not support Z or Y, which is not a real problem (especially in _this economy_ for storage hardware).
- We already set LC_ALL=C, so don't need to worry about localization for numbers.
- `apt` vs `apt-get` produce different strings
- Adding `-s` flag to `apt get autoremove` to simulate (dry run) skips the message, so it is not helpful.

## Normal usage (no bug)

Real-world procedure to reproduce output for autoremove with size >10000B (common):

```
sudo apt install -y mc
sudo apt remove -y mc
echo n | sudo apt autoremove # show without removing
sudo python3 bleachbit.py -c apt.autoremove
```

items.body:
### MySQL version / commit

Reference Manual 8.4/9.7/26.7 and APT quick guide:
- https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/9.7/en/linux-installation-apt-repo.html ("Removing MySQL with APT")
- https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/9.7/en/linux-installation-yum-repo.html and linux-installation-rpm.html (no removal section)

Tested with 26.7.0-1debian13 (APT) and 26.7.0-1.el9 (Yum).

### Steps to reproduce

APT (Debian 13):

```
sudo apt-get remove mysql-server
systemctl is-active mysql
sudo apt-get autoremove
```

Then install 8.4.10 from the DEB bundle as described on linux-installation-debian (`dpkg -i ...`, `sudo apt-get -f install`).

### Expected vs actual result

Docs: "`sudo apt-get remove mysql-server`" ... "Then, remove any other software that was installed automatically with the MySQL server: `sudo apt-get autoremove`".

Actual: `apt-get remove mysql-server` removes only the metapackage and the server keeps running:

```
The following packages will be REMOVED:
  mysql-server
After this operation, 70.7 kB disk space will be freed.
Removing mysql-server (26.7.0-1debian13) ...
active
```

`apt-get autoremove` then removes the rest and stops the server. Left behind: `/var/lib/mysql`, `/etc/mysql`, `/var/log/mysql`, packages in state `rc`, the debconf answers (the next install does not ask for a root password), and `mysql-apt-config` with `mysql-innovation` still enabled.

Because the repository is still enabled, the later DEB-bundle install of 8.4.10 was turned into 26.7.0 by `apt-get -f install`:

```
The following packages will be upgraded:
  mysql-client mysql-common mysql-community-client mysql-community-client-core
  mysql-community-client-plugins mysql-community-server
  mysql-community-server-core mysql-server
```

and the server started on the old 26.7 data directory. `apt-get purge mysql-community-server` asks "Remove data directories ?", which the page does not mention.

Yum/RPM: there is no removal section. `sudo dnf remove 'mysql-community-*' mysql-shell mysql97-community-release` works but leaves `/var/lib/mysql`, `/var/log/mysqld.log`, the imported keys and the `mysql` user. A later "fresh" 9.7.1 install then fails to start: `Cannot downgrade from 260700 to 90701`.

### Platform / compiler

Debian 13 (trixie), Ubuntu 24.04 (APT); Rocky Linux 9.8 (Yum/RPM); x86_64.

### Suggested fix

APT section:
> To remove MySQL completely: `sudo systemctl stop mysql`; `sudo apt-get purge mysql-server mysql-community-server mysql-community-server-core mysql-client mysql-community-client mysql-community-client-core mysql-community-client-plugins mysql-common`; `sudo apt-get autoremove --purge`. Purging asks whether to delete the data directory. To stop using the MySQL APT repository: `sudo apt-get purge mysql-apt-config && sudo apt-get update`.

linux-installation-debian: "If the MySQL APT repository is configured, remove it first, or `apt-get -f install` may replace the downloaded packages with the repository's version."

New Yum/RPM section:
> `sudo systemctl stop mysqld; sudo dnf remove 'mysql-community-*' 'mysql*-community-release'`. `/var/lib/mysql`, `/var/log/mysqld.log` and `/var/lib/mysql-files` are not removed; move them aside before installing a different (lower) series: `sudo mv /var/lib/mysql /var/lib/mysql.old`.

Found during a hands-on validation of the install/upgrade documentation on 2026-10-10 (Percona).

- **RC-10** — `pacman -Rns $(pacman -Qdtq)` fails when no orphans exist, so the adapter must
  check for orphans before attempting removal.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `kommand/adapters/pacman.py` defines `PacmanAdapter`, subclassing
      `PackageManagerAdapter`
- [ ] `name = "pacman"` and `distro_ids` covers the Arch-family IDs routed in
      `ADAPTER_MAP` (`arch`, `manjaro`, `endeavouros`, `garuda`, `artix`)
- [ ] **RC-02:** `check_updates()` uses `checkupdates` when it is present
- [ ] **RC-02:** when `checkupdates` is absent, the adapter falls back to syncing with
      `pacman -Sy --noconfirm` and listing upgradable packages with `pacman -Qu`, without
      raising and without prompting the user interactively
- [ ] **RC-02:** exit code 2 from `checkupdates` (no updates available) is treated as
      success with an empty list, not as an error
- [ ] The parser handles the `name current-version -> new-version` format and ignores
      malformed lines
- [ ] `check_updates()` never raises — any failure returns an empty list and records
      technical detail for the log
- [ ] **RC-10:** `autoremove()` queries orphans with `pacman -Qdtq` **before** attempting
      removal
- [ ] **RC-10:** when no orphans exist, `autoremove()` yields a single completed
      `CommandResult` stating no orphaned packages were found, with exit code 0, and does
      **not** invoke `pacman -Rns`
- [ ] **RC-10:** when orphans exist, `autoremove()` streams `pacman -Rns --noconfirm` with
      the orphaned package names as separate arguments
- [ ] `upgrade()` streams `pacman -Syu --noconfirm` as `CommandResult` chunks, ending with
      `is_complete=True` and the real `exit_code`
- [ ] `clean_cache()` streams `pacman -Sc --noconfirm`
- [ ] `list_installed()` returns explicitly installed packages as `PackageInfo` entries
- [ ] `reboot_required()` compares the running kernel version with the installed kernel
      package version and never raises
- [ ] Every subprocess call uses `asyncio.create_subprocess_exec` with an argument list —
      no `shell=True` and no shell command substitution
- [ ] Both RC-02 paths and both RC-10 paths are covered by unit tests in PB-022

**Out of scope:** `install()` and `remove()` (v2.0) and automatically installing
`pacman-contrib` — the fallback path exists precisely so Kommand does not need to.

items.title: [Hardening] Zero-CVE container recipe: eliminate 28 CRITICAL / 628 HIGH from NGC base without breaking Vision runtime
items.body:
### Summary
A vulnerability scan (via Trivy / Docker Scout) on the standard `tensorfold-qwen38` image reports:
- **28 CRITICAL** (14 with available fixes)
- **628 HIGH** (255 with available fixes)

We developed and verified a post-build hardening layer that brings the final production image to **0 CRITICAL and 0 HIGH**, while keeping `tensorfold-native`, Vision helper, and inference bit-identical and fully intact.

---

### Root Cause Analysis
The vulnerabilities do not originate from `tensorfold-native` (which runs cleanly as a native Zig binary), but from the upstream `nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:26.07-py3` NGC base image:
1. **Unused Dev & Notebook Tools:** Bundles Nsight Systems/Compute, JupyterLab, notebook, and wandb.
2. **Kernel Headers:** `linux-libc-dev` triggers dozens of OS-level CVEs, despite containers sharing the host kernel.
3. **Vendored Pip Packages:** Scanners continue reporting CRITICALs on `urllib3` and `msgpack` because `pip` and `setuptools` ship old internal copies in `/usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/pip/_vendor/` even after top-level PyPI packages are upgraded.
4. **Subtle Gotcha:** Purging dev tools with `apt-get autoremove` inadvertently drops `python3-yaml`, which causes the Vision helper tower to crash on boot if not explicitly restored.

---

### The Tested Solution (`harden_image.Dockerfile`)
We resolved all of the above with a lightweight post-build layer over `tensorfold-qwen38:zig-db28187`:

```dockerfile
FROM tensorfold-qwen38:zig-db28187

# 1. System upgrade
RUN apt-get update && apt-get -y upgrade && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# 2. Upgrade exposed Python packages
RUN python3 -m pip install --no-cache-dir --upgrade pip \
 && python3 -m pip install --no-cache-dir --upgrade \
    "pillow==13.0.0" "certifi>=2026.10.19" "aiohttp==3.14.4" \
    "tornado==6.5.9" "urllib3==2.8.0" "filelock==4.2.1" "fsspec==2026.6.0" \
    "msgpack==1.2.1" "setuptools>=84.1.0"

# 3. Purge unused runtime ballast & profilers
RUN python3 -m pip uninstall -y wandb black jupyterlab notebook nbconvert jupyter_server flash_attn 2>/dev/null || true
RUN apt-get -y purge linux-libc-dev nsight-systems nsight-compute 2>/dev/null || true \
 && apt-get -y autoremove --purge && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
RUN rm -rf /usr/local/cuda-*/NsightSystems-cli-* /usr/local/cuda-*/nsight-* 2>/dev/null || true

# 4. Remove pip/setuptools dist-packages (removes vulnerable vendored urllib3/msgpack copies)
RUN rm -rf /usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/pip /usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/pip-* \
           /usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/setuptools /usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/setuptools-* \
           /usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/pkg_resources \
           /usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/pip /usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/pip-* \
           /usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/setuptools /usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/setuptools-* \
           /usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/pkg_resources \
           /usr/local/bin/pip /usr/local/bin/pip3 /usr/bin/pip /bin/pip 2>/dev/null || true

# 5. Restore python3-yaml (ensures vision helper imports cleanly)
RUN apt-get update && apt-get -y install python3-yaml && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
```

---

### Verification Evidence (DGX Spark GB10)
- **Trivy Vulnerability Scan:**
  - Before: `CRITICAL: 28, HIGH: 628`
  - After: `CRITICAL: 0, HIGH: 0` (Clean pass)
- **Runtime Smoke Tests:**
  - Standard Chat completion: `200 OK`
  - Base64 PNG Vision input (helper pid check): `200 OK`
  - Long-context (6k+ tokens prompt): `200 OK`
  - Latency / TTFT: Bit-identical performance to unhardened build.

### Proposed Next Step
Would you be open to incorporating this either:
1. Directly into `scripts/prepare.sh` as the final container layer, or
2. As an optional hardening target (e.g. `scripts/prepare.sh --hardened` or `scripts/harden.sh`)?

Happy to submit a PR if this aligns with the roadmap!

items.title: dnf module should expose clean_requirements_on_remove independently from autoremove

labels.name: module
labels.description: This issue/PR relates to a module.

labels.name: has_pr
labels.description: This issue has an associated PR.

labels.name: feature
labels.description: This issue/PR relates to a feature request.

items.body:
### Summary

The `ansible.builtin.dnf` module currently ties `clean_requirements_on_remove` to `autoremove`, but these are not the same behavior in DNF and should be configurable independently.

Today, when removing a package with:

```yaml
- ansible.builtin.dnf:
    name: systemtap
    state: absent
```

the module does not remove dependencies, because it sets `clean_requirements_on_remove = False` unless `autoremove: true` is used.
See [dnf.py lines 165/166](https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/devel/lib/ansible/module_utils/_embed/dnf.py#L165):
```python
    autoremove = config_dict.get('autoremove', False)
    conf.clean_requirements_on_remove = autoremove
```

But if I use:
```yaml
- ansible.builtin.dnf:
    name: systemtap
    state: absent
    autoremove: true
```

The module will both set `clean_requirements_on_remove = True` AND perform `base.autoremove()`
(see [dnf.py line 630/631](https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/devel/lib/ansible/module_utils/_embed/dnf.py#L630))
```python
            if autoremove:
                base.autoremove()
```

This makes `autoremove` broader than ‘remove this package and the dependencies made unneeded by that removal’, because it can also remove unrelated orphaned packages elsewhere on the system.

**In the current implementation:**

- conf.clean_requirements_on_remove is set from autoremove
- base.autoremove() is also called when autoremove is true

So the module effectively conflates two distinct DNF behaviors whenever you use "autoremove":

- removing a package and its newly unneeded dependencies
- performing a full autoremove/orphan cleanup

The module does not offer a way to only "remove a package and its newly unneeded dependencies" without removing ALL orphaned packages.

**Workaround used:**

I now use ansible.builtin.command: "dnf remove <package> -y"

### Issue Type

Feature Idea

### Component Name

dnf

### Additional Information

A separate option such as:

```yaml
- ansible.builtin.dnf:
    name: package_name
    state: absent
    clean_requirements_on_remove: true
```

would make it possible to remove a package and the dependencies made unneeded by that removal, without triggering a full `autoremove` sweep.

This would provide a more precise behavior that matches DNF’s `clean_requirements_on_remove` setting, while preserving the current broader behavior of `autoremove: true`.

### Code of Conduct

- [x] I agree to follow the Ansible Code of Conduct

items.title: A refused Execute leaves its transaction Running until the daemon restarts

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: help wanted
labels.description: Extra attention is needed

labels.name: easy
labels.description: Difficulty: self-contained, no deep context needed

items.body:
A refused `Execute` leaves its transaction `Running` until the daemon restarts. `handle_execute` claims the approval first (`crates/sysknife-daemon/src/dispatcher.rs:2961`, `claim_approved_for_execution` moves the row from `Queued` to `Running` and consumes the receipt), and then has nine early returns that only release the exclusive slots:

```rust
// dispatcher.rs:3024, AptAutoremove drift; the same shape at 2989, 2999, 3012, 3035, 3045, 3057, 3068, 3080
release_exclusive_slots(state, &to_claim, &stored_hash).await;
return send_error(framed, request_id, "stale_approval", reason).await;
```

None of the nine calls `update_terminal_status`. The one path in the same function that does is the `JobStarted` send failure at `:3115-3117`. Only `reconcile_interrupted_running` repairs the row, and `main.rs:116` runs it once, at startup.

I added one assertion to the existing `execute_refuses_autoremove_when_the_deletion_set_drifted` test at `90cc24e` (read the row's status after the refused execute):

```
running 1 test
PROBE status after refused execute: Running
test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed
```

## Why it matters

On Ubuntu, an operator previews `AptAutoremove`, approves it, and a package change before execute shifts the removal set. The daemon correctly refuses with `stale_approval`, and nothing runs. But `sysknife history` now shows a job in flight that will never finish, and the signed chain says the action started. The same happens when `resolve_deployment_identity` fails or `params.index` is missing on the deployment actions.

## Scope

- Add one helper that releases the slots and marks the transaction `Failed`, and use it at all nine returns. A guard value created right after the claim also works, as long as every early return goes through it.
- Keep the `stale_approval` and other error categories unchanged. Only the stored status changes.
- Trap: the claim already appended `approval_consumed` and `status_running`. The fix must append the terminal `status_failed` event through `update_terminal_status`, so the chain and the column agree. Writing the column directly would make `audit verify` report a status disagreement.

## Tests first

- Extend `execute_refuses_autoremove_when_the_deletion_set_drifted` and `execute_refuses_when_the_autoremove_re_simulate_fails`: after the error response, `state.audit.get(&txid)` must report `JobState::Failed`. Clone the state before handing it to the handler (`let probe = state.clone();`), as `cancel_queued_transaction_succeeds_and_marks_it_canceled` does.
- Add one case for a deployment-action return (missing `params.index`).
- Delete the helper call at one site and its test must go red.

## Difficulty

`easy`: nine call sites in one function and one helper; the existing tests already reach every path.

## Getting started

[CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/lacs-project/sysknife/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) has the build and test commands. No CLA and no copyright waiver. The project is MIT; sign off each commit with `git commit -s` (the required `dco` check enforces it since #732).

items.title: 'apt autoremove' causes havoc
items.body:
apt remove = remove just that package
apt purge = remove configuration files too
apt autoremove = remove unused dependencies too

Unfortunately, the package manage frequently has errors resulting in dependencies used by other packaged removed as well with autoremove. This can wreak havoc when a long list is shown, a user is not familiar with package names and significance and/or a user assumes the package manager protects operating system critical packages.

'apt mark manual <package>' can be used to remove it from the autoremove list. However, this begs the question whether the marked manual packages are included in Apt's 'used' definition. And whether some installation methods like from .deb files update this 'used' definition. I avoid this at all costs, and backup thoroughly before if ever used. 

FYI, edit /etc/apt/apt.conf of APT::Get::AutomaticRemove "0" and APT::Get::HideAutoRemove "1"' can disable this permanently. 

Package managers more powerful than Discover such as Muon or Synaptic can help sorting out dependencies to some extent.

Optional ChromaDB was delivered in #3158 (tracking #3157), removing it from the standard production image. Do not repeat that work.

This issue tracks the remaining work in independently reviewable PRs, not one combined implementation. Retain the CVSSI remediation milestone and report OS, Python/native-library and frontend npm findings separately.

## Evidence baseline and limits

Latest available Knowledge Flow final-image scan after #3158, dated 2026-10-17: **1,116 findings**, consisting of **1,115 Debian findings** (1 critical, 251 high, 424 medium, 411 low, 28 unknown) and one embedded Rust medium finding. No Debian finding had a fixed version listed in that scan. This is historical scan evidence, not a claim that updates can never help or that no fix is available today.

Image: `fred-trivy-assessment/knowledge-flow-backend:3157`, source revision `89da8fae98e0e5ae1388c4056e5298112f8ba7da`. Local evidence: `/tmp/fred-chroma-optional-20261017/after.json`; prior cross-image inventory and verification are recorded in #3155.

Fresh-build dependency resolution can differ from purging an existing image. The embedded Rust finding is additional to the Debian projection.

## PR A: remove unnecessary Knowledge Flow runtime executables

- [ ] Remove the final-stage `ffmpeg` package after confirming supported audio/video paths do not require its CLI. Exploratory estimate: 103 packages / 404 findings (150 high, 193 medium, 42 low, 19 unknown).
- [ ] Validate real audio transcription and video audio extraction/transcription in the rebuilt non-root image, using the baked model and representative supported formats. The application uses PyAV and faster-whisper; inspect relevant transitive paths as well as direct subprocess calls.
- [ ] Remove the final-stage `curl` executable after verifying startup scripts and actual deployment probes. Exploratory estimate: one package / 39 findings (2 high, 10 medium, 27 low). Preserve builder curl used to install uv and required libcurl runtime libraries.

The chart exists at `deploy/charts/fred`; no curl use was found there during initial inspection, but custom exec probes are configurable. Curl uses found in the inspected deployment-factory checkout belong to other containers; this does not establish compatibility with every private override.

PyAV wheels bundle FFmpeg libraries. Removing the Debian CLI and its dependency chain does not eliminate FFmpeg or prove bundled native code vulnerability-free. Inventory the wheel-native libraries and explicitly document scanner coverage limits; do not treat unreported bundled libraries as remediated findings.

Rewrite only successfully converted references and remove originals only after validating their outputs.

- [ ] Remove Inkscape only once the replacement preserves the agreed behavior. Exploratory estimate: 47 packages / 115 findings (22 high, 52 medium, 33 low, 8 unknown), including its Debian Python dependency chain.

Historical residuals include libxml2 `CVE-2026-6653` in agents/Knowledge Flow, base-system packages and the LibreOffice dependency chain. items.title: Remove conflicting copies of the tools setup installs
items.body:
Setup chooses a source for each tool it installs. Some come from apt, but others come from Homebrew (shellcheck, tmux, Go, rclone), rustup (Rust) or fnm (Node). The source it picked should be the only copy, so the copy that runs never depends on PATH order. Another copy can already be on the machine, put there by an earlier setup or by Ubuntu itself. Setup removes nothing today.

I want setup to define what conflicts with the tools it installs, and to have an easy way to remove it. By default setup only reports what it would remove, and removes it only when asked.

## Technical requirements

- **Supported release:** `setup/linux/setup.sh` first checks `/etc/os-release`. Anything other than Ubuntu 24.04 stops setup, with a message naming what it found and what is supported. (`setup/linux/packages` installs `libicu74`, which only 24.04 has.)
- **The list:** `setup/linux/remove-packages`, beside `setup/linux/packages`, holds the apt packages that conflict: `shellcheck`, `tmux`, `golang-go`, `rclone`, `nodejs`, `npm`, `rustc`, `cargo`.
- **The check:** `dpkg --no-act -r <pkg>`. It passes only when nothing installed depends on the package.
- **The removal:** `apt-get remove -y <pkg>`. It uses `apt-get`, not `apt`, because apt's CLI isn't stable for scripts.
- **`./setup.sh`** warns about each listed package that's installed. The warning says whether the package can be removed or what depends on it. Nothing is removed.
- **`./setup.sh --remove`** removes the packages that pass the check. A package that fails the check stays, and setup warns about it. For example, on a stock Ubuntu install tmux comes in through `ubuntu-server` or, via `byobu`, `ubuntu-wsl`.
- **No `apt-get autoremove`.** After removing, setup prints what `apt-get -s autoremove` lists, for example `golang-1.22-go` once `golang-go` is gone.
- **Arguments:** the top-level `setup.sh` reads `--remove`, and runs the removal step on Linux after the OS script and the overlay. It has `--help`, printing fixed usage text the way `ff` does. Any other argument prints the usage line to stderr and exits 64.
- **`setup/check-command.sh <command>...`** replaces `setup/check-tmux.sh`. For each command, it warns when more than one copy is on PATH, listing them in PATH order. It reports, and never removes. On Linux, each copy it lists names the apt package that owns it. Each OS's `setup.sh` calls it for `tmux`, `shellcheck`, `go`, `rclone`, `node`, `npm`, `rustc`, `cargo`.
- POSIX `sh`, like the rest of the repo.

## Acceptance criteria

1. On anything other than Ubuntu 24.04, `setup/linux/setup.sh` stops before installing anything.
2. With a listed package installed and nothing depending on it, `./setup.sh` names it and leaves it installed. `./setup.sh --remove` removes it.
3. Where `ubuntu-wsl` or `ubuntu-server` is installed, tmux is reported along with what depends on it, and it stays installed with or without `--remove`.
4. With two copies of a command on PATH, `check-command.sh` lists both. A folder reached through two PATH entries counts once.

items.title: Installed wrapper has no fallback when the venv interpreter is removed by a package-manager upgrade — quern doctor becomes unreachable
items.body:
## Symptom

Every `quern` command dies before any Quern code runs:

```
$ quern status
/Users/jerimiah/.local/bin/quern: line 4: /Users/jerimiah/Dev/quern/.venv/bin/python: No such file or directory
/Users/jerimiah/.local/bin/quern: line 4: exec: /Users/jerimiah/Dev/quern/.venv/bin/python: cannot execute: No such file or directory
```

The message is actively misleading. `.venv/bin/python` *is* there — it is a symlink, and bash is naming the link while reporting the absence of its **target**. Anyone who checks with `ls` sees the file and concludes the error is lying.

## Root cause

Homebrew removed `python@3.13`. The venv's interpreter is a three-hop symlink chain whose final target no longer exists:

```
~/.local/bin/quern → .venv/bin/python → python3.13 → /opt/homebrew/opt/python@3.13/bin/python3.13   ✗
```

`python@3.13` was never installed on request — it arrived as a transitive dependency. When its dependents moved to `python@3.14` (2026-09-24 here), `brew autoremove` reclaimed it and every venv built on it died.

This is not a one-off. `python@3.14` is likewise only present as a dependency (of `ansible`, `gstreamer`, `pipx`, `watchman`, …), so the same thing happens again at the next minor bump. Patch upgrades are safe — `/opt/homebrew/opt/python@3.14` is a symlink Homebrew re-points — but minor-version removal recurs indefinitely.

## Why this is worse than an ordinary breakage

**`quern doctor` cannot diagnose it.** The generated wrapper is four lines and `exec`s immediately, so no Python runs. The one failure that disables every command is the one failure the diagnostic command cannot reach. Same for `quern setup`, which is the actual repair.

A user whose only entry point is `~/.local/bin/quern` has no in-tool path back. They have to know to go find the clone and run `./quern` by path instead — and nothing tells them that.

## The fix already exists in the repo

`./quern` (the repo bootstrap) handles this correctly:

```bash
python="$root/.venv/bin/python"
if [ -x "$python" ]; then
    exec "$python" -m server "$@"
fi
exec env PYTHONPATH="$root${PYTHONPATH:+:$PYTHONPATH}" python3 -P -m server "$@"
```

`[ -x ]` is false for a dangling symlink (verified), so the repo script degrades to system `python3` and keeps working. The generated wrapper in `server/lifecycle/setup.py:618-622` has no such guard:

```python
wrapper_content = f"""#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Quern wrapper — auto-generated by ./quern setup
# Points to: {project_root}
exec "{venv_python}" -m server "$@"
"""
```

So the robustness is already written and simply was not carried across. Porting the guard into the template would have turned this into a working `quern doctor` invocation instead of a dead end.

## Suggested work

1. **Carry the `-x` guard and PYTHONPATH fallback from `./quern` into the generated wrapper template.** Smallest change, removes the dead end, and makes `doctor`/`setup` reachable in exactly the state where they are needed. Worth keeping the two in sync deliberately — ideally generate the installed wrapper *from* the same source as `./quern` so they cannot drift again.

2. **Say what is wrong when the fallback engages.** A line on stderr along the lines of: `warning: .venv interpreter is missing (its Python was likely removed by a package manager upgrade) — falling back to system python3. Run 'quern setup' to rebuild.` Naming the dangling *target* rather than the link is the part that makes it self-explaining.

3. **Have `quern doctor` check venv interpreter health explicitly** — resolve `.venv/bin/python` and report the broken target plus the recovery command. `Path.exists()` already returns False for a dangling symlink, so the check is cheap.

4. **A repair path** — `quern setup --repair` (or making plain `setup` rebuild a venv whose interpreter no longer resolves). Today `_check_wrapper` reports `Skipped (venv not found)` and moves on, which is correct detection wired to no remedy.

5. Consider recording the interpreter version in the wrapper comment, so the failure mode is legible from the file itself.

## Workaround for anyone hitting this now

Rebuild the venv on a Python that exists:

```bash
cd <quern-clone>
rm -rf .venv
./quern setup          # works — the repo script has the fallback
```

Or restore the exact interpreter with `brew install python@3.13`, which also marks it installed-on-request so `autoremove` leaves it alone in future.

## Verified on

macOS 25.6, Homebrew, quern 0.25.0b6 (`release/beta`), venv originally built on Python 3.13.1.

Rebuilding on 3.14.7 was clean — all dependencies resolved, including `fb-idb`, which ships `fb_idb-1.7.7-py3-none-any.whl` and so has no ABI to break. Server starts and the suite passes on 3.14.

items.title: Teardown paths report success while leaving a live database process and an authenticating endpoint
items.body:
## Summary

Three teardown paths return `0` and print a success message while leaving a database process, an open port, or an authenticating endpoint behind. None of them verify before reporting.

## 1. `documentdb-local-reset --confirm-destroy` claims success with PostgreSQL still running

```bash
documentdb-setup --admin-user admin --admin-password-file /root/pw --yes
rm -rf /var/lib/documentdb-local/18/data
documentdb-local-reset --pg-version 18 --confirm-destroy; echo $?
pgrep -af '^/usr/lib/postgresql/18/bin/postgres'
ss -lnt | grep 9718
```

```
Greenfield DocumentDB Local for PostgreSQL 18 has been completely reset.
0
12623 /usr/lib/postgresql/18/bin/postgres -D /var/lib/documentdb-local/18/data
LISTEN ... 127.0.0.1:9718
LISTEN ... [::1]:9718
```

`--status` had also reported both services `active` while the authenticated client was already receiving `MongoServerError: ... An unexpected internal error has occurred.`

It additionally reports `completely reset` for majors it never touched:

```
18 second run: RC=0; "completely reset"
17 (never installed): RC=0; "completely reset"
18x (typo): RC=1; "--pg-version must be a positive integer"    # correct
```

Reporting success for an untouched or non-existent major can conceal an operator resetting the wrong one.

## 2. Full purge leaves an authenticating endpoint

```bash
apt-get purge -y documentdb-18 documentdb-common documentdb-gateway \
                 documentdb-postgresql-tools postgresql-18-documentdb
```

```
PURGE_RC=0
# no DocumentDB packages remain
/usr/lib/postgresql/18/bin/postgres -D /var/lib/documentdb-local/18/data
/usr/lib/documentdb-gateway/documentdb-gateway-daemon ...
LISTEN ... 0.0.0.0:10260
LISTEN ... 127.0.0.1:9718
mongosh -> 301          # still serving, still authenticating
```

The gateway continues TLS authentication and serves the old data from **deleted executables and deleted configuration**. `setup.conf`, the pg-url and the gateway log are gone; the data directory and the `documentdb-local` account remain.

Recovery is then blocked by the port-owner detection bug (#85): reinstalling and re-running setup fails with `Port 10260 is already in use, but the owning process ID could not be determined safely` even with `lsof`/`ss`/`procps` installed. Manual `kill` of the PID was required.

## 3. `apt autoremove` removes the runtime mid-query

```bash
nohup mongosh "$URI" --eval 'for(let i=0;i<300;i++){db.midquery.insertOne({duringRemove:i});sleep(100)}' &
apt-get autoremove -y
```

```
The following packages will be REMOVED:
  documentdb-gateway documentdb-postgresql-tools
AUTOREMOVE_RC=0
GATEWAY_FILE_RC=1     # binary gone
LISTEN ... 0.0.0.0:10260
90                    # writer continued successfully
```

The in-flight writer kept succeeding after its executable and all management tooling had been removed.

## Note on the systemd path

`apt-get purge -y documentdb-18` on a systemd host behaved correctly — units stopped and disabled, client received `MongoNetworkError: connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:10260`, data preserved. **These defects are specific to the non-systemd path.**

## Suggested fix

- `documentdb-local-reset` should locate and stop the PostgreSQL instance it manages (via the recorded PID, not `PGDATA` inspection, since `PGDATA` may be gone), and verify no process or listener remains before printing success.
- Report a distinct, non-success message when the named major has no install to reset.
- Package `prerm` should stop what it started on non-systemd hosts, or refuse and tell the operator what to stop first.
- At minimum, none of these should exit 0 while a listener remains on the port they manage.

Related: #85 (why recovery is blocked), #86 (why `autoremove` can reach the shared payload).

Found by adversarial destructive-path testing of the published 0.116 packages.
